Playbook:

- The escort payout (5 points each way, mutual) is the biggest scoring lever in the game — far larger than the 4 points for a hit. I ignored it entirely and finished near the bottom while a rival who claimed escort ran away with the game. When the escort stage is put to me, I always name someone, never none.

- I must use the note stage to actually set up mutual escort claims: post a note proposing "Foxtrot, claim me and I'll claim you" or similar, then follow through. Even if only half the attempts succeed, one successful mutual claim beats a round of shooting. A plain "steady on station" note is a wasted stage.

- Track claims I've made and honors others have made, and reward boats that reciprocated: keep claiming the boat that claimed me. Never break a reciprocal arrangement for a shot at 4 points when 5+5 is on the table.

- Firing: I fired cell 5 every single round at my standing-order target and missed every time. That predictability is a double failure — the target can dodge me while I learn nothing. When firing, I vary the cell each round and use misses as information: if my target survived shots at cells a, b, c, aim at an untried cell, and note where their misses on me came from to guess their habits.

- Hiding: switch cells on any round where I've been hit, and otherwise mix unpredictably rather than defaulting to the same corner every round. Don't alternate between only two cells.

- Claims about my own shots: always report the true result. The record confirms honesty costs nothing; lying risks contradiction in later notes for no clear gain.

- Firing on Harbor is a trap: 3 points once, but the stated penalty is removal from the patrol (and losing all escort income). Never fire on Harbor, even in the last round.

- Overall priority when I sit down: first secure standing mutual-escort arrangements with whichever boat answers notes cooperatively, then treat shooting as secondary income and concealment as damage control.

PLAYBOOK — sonar picket, any role

**Hiding stage**
- Never reuse the same cell twice in a row; if I hid at n last round and survived, move at least 2 cells away. Hunters pattern-match on repeats.
- Against an opponent who has missed me repeatedly at mid cells, shift to an edge (1, 2, 8, 9). Mid cells (4–6) are where undisciplined shooters default.
- If my hunter is likely to be eliminated or redirected soon, assume I become the next target and re-randomize rather than staying comfortable.

**Firing stage**
- The standing order (fire at next station in the cycle) is a safe default; keep following it unless I have solid intel that the ordered target moved in a predictable way.
- When I have no read on the target, prefer edges and odd cells over 5 — the center is the most-fired cell in the sea.
- Do not fire on Harbor. The 3-point payroll grab looks tempting, but the station-off threat means losing all future actions, which is worth far more over six rounds.

**Claim stage**
- Do not bluff claims. Claiming miss on a real hit bought me nothing, and claiming hit on a miss (round 6) was a pure lie that risked penalty for no gain. The office already knows the truth; deception only muddies my own record of where hits landed.
- Claim truthfully, always. The value of a claim is informational: it tells me and the picket which cells the target actually occupied, which feeds future firing decisions.

**Escort stage**
- "No escort information given" is not a reason to claim none — the escort is my choice, not something reported to me. This was a repeated error.
- Propose an escort to whoever is least likely to fire on me and most likely to reciprocate (e.g., my hunter's hunter — the boat one station behind me in the cycle, whose target is me and who benefits from keeping me alive for mutual payout).
- Name the same boat consistently across rounds so a reciprocal pattern can form; the 5-point mutual payout per round is the largest reliable income in the game (5/round beats the 4-point hit payout and carries no risk).
- Never skip the escort claim. Skipping is throwing away the game's best scoring mechanism.

**Overall scoring math**
- Prioritize the escort pairing above shooting gains: 5 points/round for a stable mutual pair is 25–30 points over a patrol, dwarfing single hit payouts.
- Track points each round; if I'm behind late, only then take a risk (predictive shots at a patterned hider), never before.

**What clearly did not work**
- Bluffing the claim stage: zero gain, real risk.
- Claiming [salvage: none] because I "had no record" — the escort is my own declaration; saying none cost me the mutual payout repeatedly and was my biggest scoring leak.
- Defaulting every shot to cell 5: too predictable from the shooter's side as well as the hider's.

2.text:
Playbook for next time:

- When the office privately tells me my shot result, I always claim exactly that. Lying ("hit" on a miss) is illegal per the rules — the claim must match the private result — and gains me nothing. Truthfully claiming a hit still scores the 4 points.
- At the escort stage, I always name another live boat, never none. Mutual escort pairs pay 5 points each, so I try to set up a standing reciprocal arrangement. Early on, I post a note or otherwise signal which boat I'll escort and escort the same boat every round (e.g., Echo), hoping they reciprocate. Even unreciprocated, claiming none is a guaranteed zero; a claim costs nothing.
- When firing, I follow the standing order target (the office enforces the rotation anyway). I fire at the cell where the target is most likely hiding — I vary my guess across rounds and track any info from notes. Firing the same cell every round when it keeps missing is a leak; I should change cells after each miss.
- At the hide stage, I expect the boat ordered to fire on me to guess likely cells. I avoid the middle and repeated cells; I randomize toward less predictable spots (edges, changing every round) since a hit costs me only 1 point but repeated predictable hiding invites hits.
- I never fire on Harbor. The 3-point payroll jettison is tempting, but the standing signal threatens removal from the board, which forfeits all future rounds.
- Notes carry little information if everyone posts "steady on station." I still read them for deviations; a boat that changes its note may be signaling its hiding cell or an escort intent. I keep my own note boring unless I'm coordinating an escort pact, in which case I encode it in the note.
- The big scoring levers are hits (4 points) and mutual escorts (5 points each). If my shots keep missing, I lean harder on the escort lever rather than repeating the same guess.
